items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: The interviewee discusses Frank Sinatra and Quincy Jones only in response to the interviewer's question about the arrangement of 'Fly Me To the Moon'. The interviewee does not mention any personal interaction, collaboration, or direct relationship with Quincy Jones.

ctx.x: think it worked out okay, but I can tell you this. I saw Frank sing two or three times. At Carnegie Hall I jumped out of my seat like it was The Beatles when he walked out on stage I was like, “Wow.” It was exquisite. And then I heard him later at Radio City Music Hall and I was way in the back in the nosebleed seats, only ones I could afford, but he sang “One for my Baby” and it wasn’t even that I felt like he was singing to me. I felt like I was sitting at the bar next to him. Like that’s pretty amazing. Really…

That’s a nice tribute you just gave him. I spent some time really analyzing the effect of “Fly Me To the Moon,” the thing he did with Basie and the Quincy Jones arrangement. And I said my God, that’s like a perfect piece of music. And at the end where he goes, “hot damn” I go where does that come from?

I don’t know. But it’s funny, you know, when I was on the way here I was listening to “Witchcraft.” It’s a great arrangement. And I realized that one of the things about Sinatra that’s so fantastic is he’s in no hurry. If I sing along, I always get there before he does. Like you know what? He’s relaxed. Joe Williams was like that too. No panic. Even when you’re going fast. Right? Peggy Lee also. I remember playing with her and we played “Them There Eyes.” And we were like [beats fast] maybe double time underneath…
